notes.title: Major Update: Cloud Saves + Free Surface Movement
notes.content:
[b]Cloud Save:[/b] With the new cloud save feature, you can upload your save games to share your unique systems with the community or download other players' creations.

[b]Explore Freely:[/b] You can now freely explore the surfaces of all planets! Move around and check out the planetary terrain. Mars, Earth, the Moon and the Jovian Moons have highly realistic terrain based on real planetary terrain data from space agencies. 

[b]Change Object Shape: [/b] You can now alter the axial proportions of objects, making them flatter or wider as you desire. This allows you to make objects more elongated to simulate extreme gravitational pull or rotational speed. Or just to create a fun "Flat Earth"!

- Besides "cracking" an object to split it in a number of pieces, you can now also turn it into a particle ball of thousands of particles that react to gravity. This option can be set from the physics menu.
- Planet debris from collisions is now susceptible to gravity. Collisions will now leave visible craters on the surviving body
- Besides a ring shape, you can now also set particle rings to a donut or sphere shape
- You can now set the eccentricty of orbits with the use of the orbit helper
- The orbit helper can now assist in setting up binary orbits
- You can change the skybox to a custom design of your choice. To have the least distortion, try using an equirectangular panoramic 360 image
-  Added 3 well-known galaxies in their correct locations: Sombrero Galaxy, Sculptor Galaxy and Whirlpool Galaxy
- You can now also set object parameters directly by clicking on them and using the keyboard instead of only using the sliders
- You can turn planet surfaces into crater landscapes by adding a bunch of random craters to them

notes.title: Update 0.285
notes.content:
1. From now on, you can create custom particle ring systems which respond to gravity and add them to planets.

2. You can now change celestial bodies into particle balls, simulating the loss of gravitational cohesion (Roche limit breakup)

3. Eclipses will make the sky turn darker now.

- Gas giants will now have counter-rotating cloud bands. On a fast spinning planet they could be hard to see, but you can slow down the rotation using the axis menu to see the cloud swirls! 
- New brown dwarf model, the goal was to have something between a planet and a star.
- Planets will now automatically start breaking apart when they enter the Roche limit. "Crackable planets" has to be set to ON in the physics menu for this to work.
- Bug fixes

- upgraded and more customisable accretion disk for the black hole
- When the "crackable planets" mode is on (can be set from the physics menu), there is now a continuous check if objects are within Roche limit of another object. If so, the object will start breaking apart
- Various bug fiixes

notes.title: new Version 0.266
notes.content:
- Added historic past and future events that you can load directly: comet flybys, solar eclipses and lunar eclipses. You can load them from either the start screen or from the restart menu.
- Added the blue giants Achernar, Acrux, and Hadar, as well as the red giant Aldebaran, in their correct Milky Way locations.
- Added custom clouds (textures menu p.6).  It gives some control over the shape, color and movement of the clouds.

- Added crackable planets. You can activate the "crackable planets" mode from the physics menu
- Added relativistic jet / beam in the customization menu
- Added neutron star surface in the customization menu
- Added "Darkstar aura" in the customization menu
- Added Customizable galaxy textures: you can now import the galaxy textures of your choice into the game. A good source are the images taken by Hubble: https://esahubble.org/images/archive/category/galaxies/
